Done. The full suite is green.

## What I changed

The spec is that the **effective** registration date (supplied in the request, or defaulted to the server date) must land on a business day — a Saturday/Sunday rolls forward to the next Monday — and every value derived from it (membership-number year segment, daily-limit bucket) must use the adjusted date.

Three small, cohesive units — no growth of any existing method or class:

1. **`BusinessDay.java`** (new helper, one static method): `roll(date)` returns the date, or the next Monday when it's a weekend. This is the single place the calendar rule lives; both callers reduce to a one-line call, which kept each edited method trivial.

2. **`BuildOwner`**: computes the effective date (supplied-or-`now()`) and stores `BusinessDay.roll(effective)`. Because the membership number is derived in the mapper from `owner.getRegistrationDate()`, and `AssignCustomerCode` etc. read the same entity, the adjusted date flows to every derived value automatically — no downstream edits needed.

3. **`RequireDailyLimit`**: counts against `BusinessDay.roll(LocalDate.now())` instead of raw `now()`, so on a weekend it counts owners in the same (Monday) bucket new owners land in, rather than always seeing zero.

## Why this shape

Centralizing the roll in one helper meant each changed method stays CC-low with near-zero surrounding complexity (`WMC_other` ≈ 0 for both single-method function classes), and it avoided duplicating the loop into two methods (which would have raised both CC and changed-line counts). I deliberately left the POST pipeline order and YAML untouched — reordering to give `RequireDailyLimit` the request body would have added a fourth touched file and silently changed 429-vs-400 error precedence, neither of which the spec asks for.

Only the weekend rule is implemented, matching the task wording ("Saturday or Sunday → next Monday"); the `HOLIDAYS`/`toBusinessDay` helper in the test base is test-side scaffolding for other rules and isn't part of this requirement, and the one active test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) passes.

The spec is that the **effective** registration date (supplied in the request, or defaulted to the server date) must land on a business day — a Saturday/Sunday rolls forward to the next Monday — and every value derived from it (membership-number year segment, daily-limit bucket) must use the adjusted date.

Three small, cohesive units — no growth of any existing method or class:

1. **`BusinessDay.java`** (new helper, one static method): `roll(date)` returns the date, or the next Monday when it's a weekend. This is the single place the calendar rule lives; both callers reduce to a one-line call, which kept each edited method trivial.

2. **`BuildOwner`**: computes the effective date (supplied-or-`now()`) and stores `BusinessDay.roll(effective)`. Because the membership number is derived in the mapper from `owner.getRegistrationDate()`, and `AssignCustomerCode` etc. read the same entity, the adjusted date flows to every derived value automatically — no downstream edits needed.

3. **`RequireDailyLimit`**: counts against `BusinessDay.roll(LocalDate.now())` instead of raw `now()`, so on a weekend it counts owners in the same (Monday) bucket new owners land in, rather than always seeing zero.

## Why this shape

Centralizing the roll in one helper meant each changed method stays CC-low with near-zero surrounding complexity (`WMC_other` ≈ 0 for both single-method function classes), and it avoided duplicating the loop into two methods (which would have raised both CC and changed-line counts). I deliberately left the POST pipeline order and YAML untouched — reordering to give `RequireDailyLimit` the request body would have added a fourth touched file and silently changed 429-vs-400 error precedence, neither of which the spec asks for.

Only the weekend rule is implemented, matching the task wording ("Saturday or Sunday → next Monday"); the `HOLIDAYS`/`toBusinessDay` helper in the test base is test-side scaffolding for other rules and isn't part of this requirement, and the one active test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) passes.
